audits.title: Improvement in neonatal intensive care in Northern Ireland through sharing of audit data.
audits.standard: Agreed regional quality indicators on transfer patterns, thermoregulation, antenatal steroids and surfactant timing
audits.setting: All nine neonatal intensive care units in Northern Ireland (regional network)

cycle1.result: In utero transfers 26%; antenatal steroids 68%; normothermia on first admission (inborn) 66%; surfactant first dose within 1 hour 13%.

audits.intervention: Centralised data collection with annual confidential feedback and anonymised unit comparisons; regional consensus guidelines adopted locally.

cycle2.result: In utero transfers 42%; antenatal steroids 82%; normothermia 71%; surfactant within 1 hour 66%.

audits.other_findings: A multi-professional regional network supported agreed standards and regular evaluation.
audits.citation: Jenkins J, Alderdice F, McCall E, Neonatal Intensive Care Outcomes Research and Evaluation (NICORE) Group. Improvement in neonatal intensive care in Northern Ireland through sharing of audit data. Qual Saf Health Care. 2005;14(3):202-206. doi:10.1136/qshc.2004.010371. PMID: 15933318.

audits.title: Assessment of neonatal care in clinical training facilities in Kenya.
audits.standard: Quality indicators based on prior Kenyan work and national guidelines
audits.setting: Neonatal units of 22 public training hospitals

cycle1.result: 56.9% of records had a standard admission form; maternal HIV status documented in 674/1249 (54%); doses exceeded recommendations by >20% for penicillin (11.6%) and gentamicin (18.5%).

audits.other_findings: All hospitals had oxygen; kangaroo care available in 14/22.
audits.citation: Aluvaala J, Nyamai R, Were F, Wasunna A, Kosgei R, Karumbi J, et al.. Assessment of neonatal care in clinical training facilities in Kenya. Arch Dis Child. 2015;100(1):42-47. doi:10.1136/archdischild-2014-306423. PMID: 25138104.

audits.title: Implementation of a Neonatal Audit Tool to Drive Quality Initiatives.
audits.standard: Site-customised yes/no audit questions on care actions during daily rounds
audits.setting: Network of 11 neonatal intensive care units affiliated with Children's Hospital of Philadelphia

cycle1.result: Adherence to the audit tool was variable among and within sites.

audits.intervention: Audit tool on daily rounds refined through PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: 11.4% of tracked actions showed improvement over time.

audits.other_findings: Success depended on teamwork, local autonomy and leadership support.
audits.citation: Grayson S, McKenna K, Carroll JM, Koran J, Chuo J. Implementation of a Neonatal Audit Tool to Drive Quality Initiatives. Pediatr Qual Saf. 2019;4(6):e224. doi:10.1097/pq9.0000000000000224. PMID: 32010851.

audits.title: A systematic, standards-based, participatory assessment of a continuous quality improvement project in Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan: results for neonatal care.
audits.standard: WHO neonatal care quality assessment tool (scores 0 to 3)
audits.setting: Nine maternity hospitals in Kyrgyzstan and ten in Tajikistan

cycle1.result: Neonatal care quality suboptimal (scores 1.0-1.9) in all areas.

audits.intervention: Two-year QI project: QI teams, action plans, provider capacity building, supportive supervision and policy changes, with semi-annual collaborative meetings.

cycle2.result: Improvements in routine care (+0.4 Kyrgyzstan, +0.5 Tajikistan), sick newborn care (+0.6 both), accessibility (+0.5, +0.8) and monitoring/follow-up (+0.3, +0.9).

audits.other_findings: Hospital support services remained below good practice standards.
audits.citation: Lomauri K, Caraus T, Stepanova I, Abduvalieva S, Zakirova F, Yusupova S, et al.. A systematic, standards-based, participatory assessment of a continuous quality improvement project in Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan: results for neonatal care. J Glob Health. 2025;15:04162. doi:10.7189/jogh.15.04162. PMID: 40320817.

audits.title: Using a common data platform to facilitate audit and feedback on the quality of hospital care provided to sick newborns in Kenya.
audits.standard: Recommended items for documentation on admission and accurate gentamicin dosing
audits.setting: High-volume neonatal unit (Pumwani Maternity Hospital), Nairobi

cycle1.period: 15 months before revised NAR and A&F
cycle1.result: Gentamicin dosing accuracy in babies under 2 kg 60% (2013).

audits.intervention: Revised standardised newborn admission record (NAR) form with 13 audit and feedback meetings.

cycle2.result: Documentation scores improved overall; gentamicin dosing accuracy under 2 kg 83% (2016).

audits.other_findings: Documentation of five recommended items, including temperature, remained below 50%; 16.7% of admissions had neonatal sepsis needing antibiotics.
audits.citation: Maina M, Aluvaala J, Mwaniki P, Tosas-Auguet O, Mutinda C, Maina B, et al.. Using a common data platform to facilitate audit and feedback on the quality of hospital care provided to sick newborns in Kenya. BMJ Glob Health. 2018;3(5):e001027. doi:10.1136/bmjgh-2018-001027. PMID: 30258654.
